title: Milneburg pavilions and nightlife
summary: Punch describes Sunday dances with four or five bands at the pavilions, the Lyric Theater and an all-night club.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Tell me a little bit more about Millenburg. What went on at Millenburg?

Well, just every Sunday, four or five bands would be playing out there at different pavilions. And we'd wake our dance there from nine in the morning to six in the evening and come on in town and play dances that night. At four in the morning. And then never feel tired. I felt like that was good all the way through. And they used to have a place right there where the others were talking right there now. The Lyric Theater used to be an act of building. What was it? The London? Yeah.
That's out of a pigeon cave? What do they call it?

It was out of a little theater. Pigeon cave. They had a nightclub called E-Lights. All the musicians would meet there and get off that night. That was all night. Right there at E-Lights. Right there at the theater. They could have a theater. But it's a parking lot there now. And things like that, you know, we'd stay up all night. We didn't wear our going on one beat or anything like that. I didn't die.
What went on at Millenburg, when the people danced? What all?
Well, they just, you know, right around in the cycle. It's a pavilion, sitting out on the water, see?
Yeah, but what did the people do out there? Well, they bring the nurses and join the people.
